chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him); and al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhal, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no harm in the Muhrim (one in Ihram state) entering the bathhouse, but he should not rub his body (scrub vigorously).

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.يَتَدَلَّكُ: To rub or scrub the body vigorously

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram regarding entering the bathhouse and rubbing their body?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *al-Istibsar*, this hadith clarifies the permissibility of entering the bathhouse while in Ihram, distinguishing between mere entry and the act of vigorous rubbing (*tadalluk*). The prohibition targets the removal of hair or skin through friction, which is a known invalidator of Ihram, thereby offering practical guidance for pilgrims maintaining ritual purity without compromising their sacred state.
